answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. One operator can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital, and repeated cheating risks losing it; a quartz, basalt, or sable label earns no exemption. Audits should sample work unpredictably, since predictable checks let a sybil farm compliant results and cheat elsewhere. The defense raises the cost of attack rather than proving identities unique.
